h: Libraries, trams and a Manchester climb
p: Climbing is a full-body workout, and plenty of first-timers are surprised by how quickly the forearms tire. The trick is to use your legs to push up rather than hauling with your arms, and to rest with straight arms when you can. Have a light snack before you arrive and bring a bottle of water, then you'll be ready to give every wall a fair go. Arriving a little early gives time for harnesses and the briefing without eating into your session.

Manchester is a fab city to explore on foot after a climb. The John Rylands Library on Deansgate looks like a cathedral of books, with a Gothic reading room that wows kids and adults alike, and it's free to visit. Manchester Museum on Oxford Road has dinosaurs, Egyptian mummies and a vivarium of frogs and reptiles, again free.

If you're after food, Chinatown, with its ornate arch near Mosley Street, has loads of places to eat. Outside the city centre, Dunham Massey is a National Trust estate with a deer park, gardens and a grand house, perfect for a gentle afternoon after an energetic morning. The Metrolink tram network makes it easy to get around without a car, linking the city centre with suburbs like Altrincham, Salford Quays and beyond. Salford Quays is worth a look too, with MediaCityUK and the Imperial War Museum North across the water, free to enter and full of thought-provoking displays.
